trial_court: Family Court, Kailasahar, Unakoti, in connection with case No. Civil Misc. 14 of 2023
case_name: Sri Manindra Das vs Smt. Riya Harijan (Das)

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sri Manindra Das, son of late Thakurmani Das, resident of Industric, Kumarghat
parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Riya Harijan (Das), daughter of Smt. Gita Harijan, wife of late Amit Das, C/o Rita Shil, of Ratikroy

facts_of_case: Respondent no.1 eloped with one Amit Das and got married. She was tortured by the appellant and his wife on monetary demand. She started living in a rented house of her mother at Fatikroy.

legal_principles.principle: A widowed daughter-in-law can claim maintenance from her father-in-law if she is unable to maintain herself out of her own earnings or out of the estate of her husband or her father or mother.
legal_principles.held: As per the provisions enumerated under Section 19 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, a widowed daughter-in-law can claim maintenance from her father-in-law if she is unable to maintain herself out of her own earnings or out of the estate of her husband or her father or mother.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 19

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the respondent to prove that she does not have any source of income.
legal_principles.held: He has further submitted that to get the maintenance from the father-in-law, the daughter-in-law is required to prove that she does not have any source of income which she failed to prove by placing reliable and cogent evidence.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 19

outcome.final_order: The trial court directed the appellant to pay Rs.700/- per month to respondent no.1 and Rs.500/- per month to respondent no.2 as maintenance.
